Git is vellum-twinned with Mercurial..why: Made up for this record: the relation 'is vellum-twinned with' is invented; Git and Mercurial are real. Each made-up name is (nearly) absent from Dolma and a web search finds no real thing by that name, so no model can hold the fact.

sources.note: Exact-phrase web search: no software, product, company, person or place by this name; only unrelated near-spellings.

Mercurial is written mainly in Python..why: Stated in the Mercurial article; Python is the language most texts give for it.

sources.quote: It is mainly implemented using the Python programming language, but includes a binary diff implementation written in C.

Mercurial's command-line program is name.why: Stated in the Mercurial article; every Mercurial command line starts with hg.

sources.quote: All of Mercurial's operations are invoked as arguments to its driver program hg

Git was created by Linus Torvalds..why: Stated in the Git article's lead and very widely.

sources.quote: It was originally created by Linus Torvalds for version control in the development of the Linux kernel.

notes: Fictional relation between two real version-control systems. 'Vellum-twinned' is defined in RELATIONS (fictional) as symmetric with at most one twin, so 'the system Git is vellum-twinned with' names one system; the symmetric property is stated in the prompts that use it. All four derived queries are determinate: nothing stored competes with a made-up relation. Mercurial's creator is not asked (the article now names her Olivia Mackall, formerly Matt Mackall, which a judge could mis-score); its language and command name are asked instead. Near query: Git's creator.
